finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::tls certificate verification permanently disabled for datasource connections (`rejectunauthorized: false`), so "ssl enabled" gives no mitm protection for credentials or query data
evidence: In packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts, `createClient` builds the pg Client with `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` (the same object literal the diff modifies by adding `types`), and the decrypted password is passed in the adjacent `password: decrypt(ds.password)` line. With `rejectUnauthorized: false` and no CA/servername configured, node-postgres/TLS accepts any certificate, so enabling SSL yields encryption without server authentication — a MITM can present a self-signed cert and capture credentials and query results. The claim is accurate about the code as written; I could not run the repo-wide grep (no checkout is mounted) to confirm there is no CA-pinning path elsewhere, but nothing in the supplied datasource files provides one. Note the weakness is pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff, which only adds the `types` parser option.
